the first-line combination of IO and ChT is the new standard of care for all patients with advanced NSCLC, regardless of PD-L1 status, with the exception of those patients with EGFR or ALK mutations who are candidates for tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
the optimal first-line treatment of advanced NSCLC has yet to be defined.

the combination of pembrolizumabb plus chemotherapy should be considered the standard of care for first-line therapy for patients with advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 expression ≥ 1%, while the combination of atezolizumab plus carboplatin plus paclitaxel should be considered the treatment of choice for patients with advanced squamous NSCLC.

PD-1 plus ChT is the preferred first-line treatment option for patients with advanced NSCLC harbouring a PD-L1 expression ≥50%, while for those with PD-L1 expression <1% PD-1 plus PD-L1 or CTLA-4 is recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PD-(L) 1 blockade plus ChT should be considered as a new standard of care for patients with metastatic NSCLC and PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade is a valid treatment option for patients who are not eligible for ChT.
